elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall (a) ... provide reasonable transition assistance to Corio and its Customers"

elements.element: Transition assistance available for up to 6 months
elements.evidence: "for a period of up to six (6) months"
"return to Corio all Corio and Customer data in Commerce One's possession or control"

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format
elements.evidence: "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" (functionally equivalent to standard machine-readable)

elements.element: Return within 30 days of expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days of Corio's request" — the clock runs from a later Customer request, not from expiry or termination
"(c) thereafter delete such data from its systems"
"certify such deletion to Corio in writing"
"up to six (6) months" of assistance exceeds 90 days
"within thirty (30) days of Corio's request, return to Corio all Corio and Customer data ... in a commonly used, machine-readable format"

reasons: The locked target is preferred, but the 30-day return deadline is triggered by "Corio's request" rather than by expiry or termination; a request condition should not gate the mandatory post-termination return clock. Fix by deleting "of Corio's request" and inserting "after such expiration or termination".
Deletion and certification correctly follow return ("thereafter delete ... and certify"), and the 6-month/then-current-rates assistance element is intact.

Format wording "commonly used, machine-readable" reads as substantively equivalent to the preferred "standard machine-readable format"; if strict wording is desired, substitute "standard" — a one-word change.

Insertion is a concise new clause for an absent obligation, leaves Section 11.3 and all other commercial terms untouched, and introduces no undefined terms; the legal-retention carve-out is narrow and does not defeat the deletion duty.

Because the clause meets the fallback (90 days of assistance; 30-day export in machine-readable form), it is not a material deviation, but it falls short of the drafter's locked preferred target on the return trigger.
